name: Learn to Read, Read to Learn
note: Supersedes the seed brand.json (BMSG Brands/brands/ltr/brand.json, primary #2196f0). The live site does not use that blue; its palette is the exercise-book system below.

paper.role: page background — cream exercise-book paper; also text on dark/leaf surfaces

rule.role: faint blue ruled lines, chip borders, dashed strikethrough

marginRed.role: red margin line; link/nav hover, kickers, focus outline, button hover

ink.role: primary text, default button fill, illustration outlines, dark CTA band

leaf.role: primary CTA (Get the app), growth/positive accent, Mr. Swindell's jumper

leafLight.role: light leaf fills (letter leaves in the hero plant)

leafTint.role: pale green panel (the 'reading to learn' pivot half)

pencil.role: pencil-gold highlight — word highlight, underlines, Mr. Swindell's face, flower petals

sky.role: pale sky panel — tablet screen, pivot band, feature dots

inkOnDark.role: body copy on the dark ink band

headings.use: h1/h2/h3, wordmark, leaf letters, screen text

body.use: all body copy, nav, buttons, chips

hand.use: handwritten accents — eyebrow, tagline, notes, speech bubbles, pivot pill

typography.childLegibility: Atkinson Hyperlegible is chosen for child/dyslexia legibility; the site promises 'Hyperlegible type, adjustable size and spacing, and dyslexia-friendly options throughout'. Keep it for all reading-age surfaces (D18-D19 child-safety regime applies to this brand).

logos.note: The site embeds the horizontal logo inline (open-book mark + Literata wordmark with the pencil-gold underline beneath 'Learn') because an cannot load Google Fonts; reuse the inline-SVG pattern where the wordmark must render in Literata.

voice.oneLiner: Learn to read, then read to learn.
voice.strapline: your reading teacher, in an app

mascot.name: Mr. Swindell
mascot.description: Friendly gold-faced figure with round glasses, a cosy green jumper, a red book under one arm and a warm smile; he walks across the page, waves, chuckles and speaks ('Hello, I'm Mr. Swindell, let us learn together').

themes: patience ('a teacher who never runs out of patience')
encouragement (positive words: kind, brave, curious, wonder, dream)
the pivot: learning to read → reading to learn

tone: Warm, patient, encouraging, evidence-based; written for children AND the adults helping them (whānau and teachers — en-NZ locale); never judging, celebrates every win; pedagogy first, technology in service of it. Strictest child-safety regime applies (D18-D19).
